title: White critical: compiled raw-290 points are added after the host-summed binary32 basis, not in the consumer association
evidence: core white_swing.rs:42 `(percent + self.percent_points)` where percent is the host basis `5 + rating`
trinity StatSystem.cpp:522-523 + Player.cpp:8255-8264: CritPercentage = (raw290 + 5.0f) + ratingBonus in binary32
ledger docs/development-ledger.md:28303-28306 claims the direct consumer adds raw 290 to a binary32 weapon-critical percent; the consumer adds it before the rating term
probe j_white_binary32.rs::defect_white_critical_adds_passive_after_host_sum_binary32_association (PASS): threshold is 825 bp where Trinity yields 824
why_tests_missed: The only discriminator test (6.06 + 2.0 -> 805) uses a basis whose association with 5.0 is exact; binary32 non-associativity needs ~1-in-5M rating values.
correction_boundary: WhiteMainHandInput must carry the binary32 terms in consumer association (e.g. the pre-rating flat+base term or rating separately) so Core evaluates (flat_raw290 + base) + rating; or record this as a deliberate host contract. Keep the single post-sum truncation.
must_not_widen: Do not admit rating/gear/extra modifiers or ranged/off-hand; do not change the draw order or white semantics beyond bumping WHITE_MAIN_HAND_SEMANTICS_VERSION.
note: Comparator is TrinityCore (emulator); magnitude 1 basis point on rare inputs. Severity low.

title: Hasted durations divide by an f64 frequency; the consumer multiplies by a binary32 period factor, so truncation lands 1 ms lower on ~0.13% of inputs
evidence: probe j_haste_duration.rs::defect_hasted_duration_f64_division_truncates_one_ms_below_binary32_consumer (PASS): cast 29405 and cooldown 29405 ms for 30000 ms at 2.02% haste, Trinity 29406
trinity Object.cpp:1809, SpellHistory.cpp:421, Spell.cpp:9213, SpellAuraEffects.cpp:1007; Unit.cpp:10978-10981
contrast: Core white swing period already uses the binary32 product (white_swing.rs:458-463) — internal inconsistency
why_tests_missed: Haste tests use round multipliers (1.25, 1.5, 2.0) where f64 division and binary32 multiplication agree.
correction_boundary: The actor timing-multiplier contract (HasteMultipliers) and the three duration scalers; if parity is desired, carry the binary32 period multiplier and compute (f32(ms) * mod) truncation, as white_swing::effective_period already does.
must_not_widen: Do not change RecoveryRatePolicy semantics, minimums, or introduce per-call rounding elsewhere; deadlines/work identity must be versioned.
note: Comparator is TrinityCore; exact host multiplier representation is a Core contract choice, so the defect is parity-only.

title: Raw-183 AtOrAbove target-health predicate uses the exact real threshold; the consumer truncates CountPctFromMaxHealth to an integer
evidence: probe j_target_health_threshold.rs::defect_target_health_at_or_above_uses_untruncated_threshold (PASS): max 1001, current 800 -> Core Hit; Trinity threshold 800 -> +100 points -> Critical
source raw-183 Initiation (193878 et al.) misc_value_1 = 80 is the AtOrAbove-80 slice
why_tests_missed: Fixtures use maximum 1000 where 80% is integral.
correction_boundary: CriticalTargetHealthPredicate::matches: compute the binary32 CountPctFromMaxHealth threshold (uint64(f32(max)*f32(pct)/100.0f)) when parity is intended; boss-scale maxima above 2^24 additionally round max to binary32.
must_not_widen: Do not admit low-health predicates, new percents, or scheduled threshold wakes.
note: Only a sub-1-HP band per crossing is affected; in Core health is continuous, so Core can also sit strictly between floor and exact threshold.

title: Raw-286 / charge recovery rates divide by (1+p/100); the consumer multiplies by 100/(p+100), so exact results truncate 1 ms low
evidence: probe j_recovery_rate.rs::holds_recovery_rate_two_source_amounts_match_consumer_product_order (PASS): 60 s with +50/+60 -> 24999 (Trinity 25000)
probe j_recovery_rate.rs::defect_recovery_rate_division_truncates_one_ms_below_consumer_product (PASS): 16.5 s +10% -> 14999 (Trinity 15000)
trinity SpellHistory.cpp:432-455, 996-1009
why_tests_missed: Tests use +100% on 10/20 s cooldowns, which is exact under both evaluations.
correction_boundary: Recovery-speed composition (cooldown_recovery_rate/charge_recharge_rate rate_factor) and time_math conversion: compute base * prod(100/(p+100)) (the consumer order) before truncation, or round-to-nearest-ms when the product is within epsilon of an integer.
must_not_widen: Do not change live-rebase semantics, the 0.01 floor, or stacking policy.
note: Single-source raw-286 amounts in 12.1.0 never diverge on authored cooldowns; two stacked sources (+50,+60) do on 1.5/3/6/15/30/60 s cooldowns.

title: Rotation resource-threshold wake uses a different f64 evaluation than combat projection, waking 1 ms after combat already satisfies the threshold
evidence: probe j_resource_projection.rs::defect_rotation_resource_wake_is_one_ms_after_combat_crossing (PASS): combat energy is 50.0 at 5000 ms but the `energy >= 50` action fires at 5001
python scan (scratch): with integral regen/thresholds ~28k (rate,basis,now,threshold) grid points wake late by 1 ms
why_tests_missed: Engine tests evaluate from now = 0 (basis == now), where both formulas coincide (e.g. 4000 ms crossing in query_integration.rs:619-681).
correction_boundary: Engine resource_projection/rotation MonotonicLinearProjection: carry the flow basis (basis_at, basis_balance, units/ms) and evaluate with the exact combat expression, or have the rotation re-check predicate at delta-1 against combat; the combat projection is the authority.
must_not_widen: Do not add polling, per-ms wake loops, or change combat projection semantics.
note: Internal Core inconsistency (no external comparator); only exact-tie crossings are affected.
